VPC foundations

The foundational private network where your compute lives.

1. Core Concept

  • A VPC is an isolated network. Subnets divide it by Availability Zone. Route tables dictate where traffic goes, separating public (internet-facing) from private (internal-only) workloads.

2. Key Services & Features

  • VPC & Subnets:
    • A VPC spans all AZs in a region.
    • A subnet is locked to exactly ONE AZ.
    • AWS reserves 5 IP addresses per subnet.
  • Internet Gateway (IGW):
    • Allows two-way traffic to the internet.
    • A subnet is 'public' ONLY if its route table points 0.0.0.0/0 to an IGW.
  • NAT Gateway:
    • Allows outbound-only internet access for private subnets.
    • Must be placed in a PUBLIC subnet.
    • Tied to a single AZ (use multiple for high availability).

3. Architecture Rules

  • Never put databases in a public subnet.
  • High Availability requires deploying resources across at least two subnets in different AZs.
  • VPC CIDR blocks cannot overlap if you intend to peer them.

4. Scenarios & Use Cases

  • EC2 instances in a private subnet need to download software updates.
    • Choose: NAT Gateway.
    • Why: It routes traffic out to the internet and returns the response, but blocks unsolicited inbound requests.
  • Design a highly available architecture.
    • Choose: Multi-AZ Subnets.
    • Why: An AZ is a distinct physical data center. Spanning subnets across AZs protects against facility failures.
